children: Tencent-backed Shanghai Enflame Technology--the last of China's "four little GPU Tigers"--soared in its trading debut, capping a wave of listings by the country's prominent artificial-intelligence chip startups.

The chip designer's shares surged 179% from its initial public offering price to 396.61 yuan in Shanghai on Friday, implying a market capitalization of 170.68 billion yuan, equivalent to $25.45 billion.
Enflame raised 6.12 billion yuan in its offering as it drew the similar levels of investor enthusiasm as its peers' debuts.
Enflame follows in the steps of Moore Threads and MetaX Integrated Circuits, which listed in Shanghai late last year, as well as Shanghai Biren Technology, which debuted in Hong Kong in early 2026.
Dubbed the "little tigers" of China's graphics processing units industry, the four firms represent part of Beijing's push to end reliance on foreign technology and nurture a "homegrown Nvidia."

Whereas foreign heavyweights dominate in the advanced chips used in AI training, Enflame primarily focuses on inference chips--specialized processors designed to handle heavy AI workloads in data centers.
Chinese tech giant Tencent Holdings is Enflame's largest shareholder with a nearly 18% stake. It is also Enflame's biggest client, contributing 84% of revenue in 2025.

Tencent's demand for AI accelerators has far exceeded the company's supply capacity, Enflame said in its IPO prospectus. It expects Tencent to remain a major revenue driver for the foreseeable future.
